name: Martial House
reason: The source term 'Martial House' (chs 756-826) was carried over unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: Martial Houses are martial institutions found across all four kingdoms, in all sizes. Joining one is distinct from joining a sect, and they run tiered entrance examinations, with courtyards assigned per cultivation level; with enough strength, a Martial House is an easier route to a quota than other paths.

name: Spatial Blade
reason: Yun Longtao's 'Sky Slashing Sword' (also rendered 'Void Slashing Sword' in the translation) was renamed 'Spatial Blade' to align with his space-themed power set (Spatial Armor), as Yun Longtao was localized as Logan.
description: Logan's signature sword, infamous for severing opponents' limbs. Contrary to expectations, Logan can form his Spatial Armor while wielding it, but in the end Zane's Formless Sword technique bats the Spatial Blade aside with ease.

name: White-Haired Priest
reason: The source epithet 'Daoist White Eyebrows' (also 'Daoist White Brow'/'White Brow Daoist') was localized as 'White-Haired Priest', replacing the Daoist cultural marker with the neutral 'Priest' while keeping the white-hair visual.
description: A powerful priest who arrives at the pyramid with his followers and whose origins Zane searches for in the Memory of the World's Will. He supervises the saint-level tribulations (in the source he presided over the West Dragon River competition), is openly disgusted by sycophants, and later schemes alongside the Holy Maiden. Appears Eps 837-964.

name: Dragon Arsenic
reason: The source term 'Dragon Arsenic' (chs 816-820) was kept unchanged in the adaptation.
description: A lethal, blue-tinged secret poison brewed by the dragon-blooded, for which no antidote or formula is known. Delivered on arrows in the mystic realm, a single touch can kill even Divine Sea Realm mighty warriors, yet Zane shrugs it off as it spreads like ink through his bloodstream.

name: Dragon-Blooded
reason: The source race name 'Dragon Bloodline Clan' was compressed to 'Dragon-Blooded' for a cleaner Western fantasy register.
description: An ancient race of dragon-blood warriors, remembered as geniuses: their young could train in the upper world and return long before ordinary warriors reached the Soul Sea Realm. Rather than surrender, they performed a blood sacrifice of billions of lives, sealing the Sacred Feather Sea and destroying the ascension path. Their preserved corpses are later possessed by Soul Sea warriors, and Zane admires the brilliance of their legacy (Eps 903-936).

name: Dragon-Blooded Archer
reason: The source descriptor 'Dragon Bloodline Archer' was rendered 'Dragon-Blooded Archer', consistent with the race name localization 'Dragon-Blooded'.
description: A reanimated Dragon-Blooded corpse wielding a semi-divine longbow on the golden sea, capable of killing four Soul Sea masters with a single black arrow. Its black shafts are the only weapons that could harm Zane during the arc (Eps 905-908).

name: Fatal Duel
reason: The adaptation coined 'Fatal Duel' as a formal name for the source's life-and-death duels held at the Luo family gathering (localized as House Lowell's Family Training Day).
description: A sanctioned duel to the death held on House Lowell's Family Training Day, where killing carries no consequence. Andrew uses it as a pretext to target Zane, while for Zane winning the Fatal Duel is his hoped-for path to freedom (Eps 10-16).

name: Principles of Forging
reason: The source manual 'Weapon Refining Ancestral Techniques' was renamed 'Principles of Forging', matching the adaptation's forging/smithing terminology.
description: A costly forging manual Zane acquires at auction through The Gilded Gavel for tens of thousands of Crystal Cubes (over 20,000 crystal stones in the source). It offers a glimpse into a grandmaster's weapon-refining techniques and underpins Zane's early forging progress (Eps 98-149).

name: Purple Flash Fist
reason: The source technique 'Purple Sandalwood Inch Punch' was renamed 'Purple Flash Fist', keeping the purple-light imagery while dropping the sandalwood cultural reference.
description: House Lowell's signature second-tier martial art and Zane's early workhorse technique, flaring with purple light on impact. Each blow is designed to inflict seven distinct internal injuries, and Zane later outgrows it after converting his Energy into Nether Essence (Eps 2-331).

name: Sky Forest
reason: The source location 'Canopy Forest' (chs 92-110) was renamed 'Sky Forest' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A demon-infested forest that for as long as anyone remembers has been home only to Demonic Grunts. The Skyreach Sect has sent disciples to hunt demons there for years, and it serves as the stage of the demon-hunting mission arc (Eps 106-124).

name: Strength Level
reason: The source's second body-cultivation stage, the 'Flesh Refinement Stage' (between Skin Refinement and Bone Refinement), was renamed 'Strength Level' to fit the adaptation's simplified Level naming.
description: An early body-cultivation stage: a warrior advances to the Strength Level and then to the Bone Refining Level. Andrew reached its peak at fourteen, while Zane barely scraped into it by sixteen; peak Strength Level practitioners gain access to basic healing skills (Eps 2-324).

name: Wind
reason: Generic capitalized token aggregating unrelated mentions (literal wind, the Wind Laws, 'Old Wind', the Heavenly Wind War Emperor, the Evil Wind Cave); not a single entity.

name: Engraved Slab
reason: The source's 'letter tablet', the device mentors use to track disciples during trials, was localized as 'Engraved Slab' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A slab-like viewing device through which masters monitor disciples remotely: mentors watch Joe and Zane during the Bloody Mountain trial through their Engraved Slabs, and Isla Novak tracks Zane's every move on one from Misty Peak (Eps 42-176).

name: Armored Wyvern
reason: The 'Five-Clawed Black Dragon' Luo Zheng forms and controls in the source battle (chs 125-127) was renamed 'Armored Wyvern', avoiding confusion with the adaptation's other dragon entities.
description: A fearsome draconic beast created and directed by Zane during the battle with Aldrich, stunning the demon that a human kid could make such a thing. Zane sends it crashing through the Light Barrier straight at Aldrich while Yolande Shaw pours her remaining Life Force into the strike (Eps 139-140).

name: Marrow Refining
reason: The source stage 'Marrow Refining (Realm/Stage)' was carried over as the 'Marrow Refining Level', matching the adaptation's Level naming for cultivation stages.
description: An advanced body-cultivation stage (per the master sheet, from Ep 62 on). Marrow Refining cultivators are strong enough that four of them thrashing Zane could purify his body, yet the stage is repeatedly dismissed as lowly by nature creatures and Infernal Peak fighters when Zane overperforms at it (Eps 18-824).

name: Array Plate
reason: The source device 'formation plate', used to control and monitor formations, was localized as 'Array Plate' ('Magic Array Plate' in the master sheet).
description: A device used to control a formation and monitor those inside it: at Emberfin Lake it tracks Zane's position without showing what is happening to him. Later, an intricately carved Array Plate is found nestled beside the Celestial Fragment in a brocade box, and it is operated by feeding Vitality into it (Eps 181-677).

name: Bloodstone Bracelet
reason: The source heirloom 'blood jade bracelet' (Mo Can's father's bracelet, taken by his Third Uncle Mo Xiuyan) was renamed 'Bloodstone Bracelet', with jade swapped for the invented material Bloodstone.
description: Ethan Grant's father's heirloom, carved from a single fist-sized piece of incredibly rare Bloodstone. It was stolen by James Moon, and its reappearance exposes his treachery; once recovered, its familiar weight on Ethan's wrist is both comforting and bittersweet (Eps 198-207).

name: Bloodstone
reason: The source material 'blood jade' was localized as 'Bloodstone' for the Western fantasy register.
description: An incredibly rare and valuable blood-red treasure material; a single fist-sized piece forms Ethan's heirloom Bloodstone Bracelet (Ep 198).

name: Weapon Pavilion
reason: The source weapons shop 'Thousand Secrets Pavilion' (Qianji Pavilion, the capital's largest weapon dealer) was renamed the plainer 'Weapon Pavilion'.
description: A bustling weapons shop in the imperial capital, its walls hung with a gleaming array of weaponry and its real treasures kept in a back section. Zane browses it with his mysterious companion under the intense scrutiny of a watching woman, while the shopkeeper plays guide (Eps 208-214).

name: Jerry
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yan Jie' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Jerry', keeping a loose phonetic echo of 'Jie'.
description: A domineering disciple at The Seventeenth Court who barks orders at the other disciples and wields a dark purple flame (the source's Real Fire). Together with his partner Mark (source Jiang Min) he tries to strong-arm Zane over the newly forged sword, but is cowed by Zane's terrifying aura and convinced Zane would kill him (Eps 217-220).

name: Kane
issues: Note: the master sheet also lists an unrelated 'Bastian Kane' (Misty Peak student, Ep 271+); the 'Kane' mentions in this dossier (Eps 227, 349) all refer to the emperor Kane Novak, not Bastian Kane. Do not merge the two.

name: Kane Novak
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Su Qian' was fully localized to 'Kane Novak'; the surname 'Novak' ties him to the imperial family (his daughter is Isla Novak, source Su Lingyun).
description: The emperor of the eastern Empire (source: the Burning Heaven Empire) and father of Isla Novak. His power rivals or exceeds the Head of the Skyreach Sect, and his membership in Cloud Hall places him above even the Sect's leader in status; the Empire has only ever produced one Kane Novak. He barely cared about running the country even while he held the throne, withdrawing into seclusion while the Crown Prince ruled in his stead (Eps 227-974).

name: Sea Peak
reason: One of the Skyreach Sect's Thirty-Three Peaks from the source's peak system; the specific source peak name behind 'Sea Peak' could not be confirmed from the evidence.
description: One of the weaker divisions of the Skyreach Sect, home to Master Silas and premier inner disciple York. After years of laying low and secretly building strength, it fields five Peak-level students among thirteen at the competition, though like Misty Peak it is lucky to qualify even its top ten (Eps 235-254).

name: Master Young
issues: Split/merge concern: 'Master Young' covers two apparently distinct characters — a Skyreach Sect master (Mack's master, who orders Richard to take Zane down and burn him, Eps 246-257; plausibly source 'Mentor Yu' of Black Rock Peak) and a Sea Wyrm Sect elder who meets Tessa and Zane and defers to Elder Shaw (Eps 686-688).
reason: The source title-name 'Mentor Yu' was localized as 'Master Young', a US-style surname with a phonetic echo of 'Yu'.
description: A sect master hostile to Zane during the Peak Competition: he is Mack's master, chats with array-designer Master Robert, and secretly instructs Richard to take Zane down within a minute and burn him, later left speechless by the Titan Strike. A separately-scened 'Master Young' of the Sea Wyrm Sect later snaps at Tessa and bristles at the respect shown to Zane (Eps 246-688).

name: Sect’s Chosen
reason: The source's 'personal disciples' (disciples taken personally by elders) were renamed the 'Sect’s Chosen', a more evocative title for the Western fantasy register.
description: The elite students personally taken on by the Skyreach Sect's Guardians and elders, standing above the ordinary disciples of the Thirty-Three Peaks. Membership is a mark of prodigy status — Patrick achieves prominence among them at only Level Two of the Adept Realm — yet at the competition only Patrick of the Chosen cracks the top five as peak disciples like Wynn, Shayna, Jason, and Jill cut the rest down (Eps 281-297).

name: Lois
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Jin Qiaoning' (Zhuo Bufan's fiancée) was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Lois', matching her fiancé's localization as Frank.
description: A tall, slender Luminous Sect disciple and Lady Sigmund's prized student, engaged to Frank through a betrothal their masters arranged three years earlier. Fiercely devoted, she regards herself as the only one worthy to stand at Frank's side and cuts down Finn with contempt on his behalf, then fights beside Frank on the Death Road, where tar-like phantoms nearly drag her under (Eps 375-403).

name: Wyatt
issues: MasterLS mismatch: the sheet lists Wyatt as a Misty Peak outer disciple named around Ep 190+, but the delivered episodes only use 'Wyatt' in Eps 39-49 for the Trial of Blood invigilator (source Zhong Ming). The MasterLS entry appears outdated or refers to an abandoned draft naming.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhong Ming' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Wyatt'.
description: The invigilator overseeing the Trial of Blood: he leaps from the Skycruiser to break up a disciple brawl (reluctant to implicate a Legacy apprentice) and announces the trial's results. Secretly corrupt, he tampers with the System Interface — erasing the circle at its core, the source's illusory array disk — to seize control of a monster and send it charging at Zane (Eps 39-49).

name: Fiery Dragon Spirit
reason: The source's 'Soul Departing Fire Dragon Essence' was simplified to 'Fiery Dragon Spirit', trimming the unwieldy literal translation.
description: A monster of pure power and the relentless guardian of the crystal key. Its lashing flames melt the ice crystals of the summoned Ice Phoenix, shrinking it with every exchange, and it fills the cave mouth with raging fire as it hunts the intruders (Eps 391-395).

name: Goddess Path
reason: The source cultivation manual 'Empyrean Fairy Heart Sutra' (Ning Yudie's technique) was renamed the 'Goddess Path', replacing the sutra framing with a Western-fantasy discipline name.
description: Cloud Hall's supreme cultivation discipline, taught to Tia by Imogen. It is grueling — Tia had to disperse her cultivation eight separate times before ascending to lead Cloud Hall — but mastery grants power far beyond one's realm: a Spirit-Tribulation Realm cultivator who completes it can fight like a Life-and-Death Realm warrior. Tia spends much of the saga working to master its final stage and recover her full strength (Eps 421-985).

name: Nightjade Fighting Soul
reason: The source soul rank 'Blue Soul Realm' was renamed the 'Nightjade Fighting Soul', with 'Fighting Soul' standardizing the source's 'Battle Soul' terminology.
description: A high rank of soul cultivation, essentially unobtainable in the Lower World — Zane's soul only ascends to it after the Cobalt Dragon plants a soul seed in him in The Heartlands. Reaching it as a fifth-level Life-and-Death Realm warrior is impressive below but unremarkable in the Upper World, where the Argent Fighting Soul marks the next great leap (Eps 441-1093).

name: Alpha
reason: The source's 'Blade Insect Leaders' (the leader caste of the blade insects, localized as Razorwings) were renamed 'Alphas', a natural English term for pack leaders.
description: The leader caste of the Razorwing swarms, far faster and stronger than ordinary Razorwings and most feared for their poisonous stingers. They coordinate the swarm with clicking mandible-language, and their crystal cores are worth many times an ordinary core — Zane deliberately baits and harvests them during the insect tide (Eps 66-74).
